title: RAPO: Expanding Exploration for LLM Agents via Retrieval-Augmented Policy Optimization

problem.claim: Existing Agentic RL methods rely on pure on-policy exploration, restricting exploration to self-generated outputs and limiting discovery of new reasoning perspectives.

gap.claim: Existing approaches using auxiliary off-policy signals typically use full off-policy trajectories for trajectory-level policy estimation and overlook fine-grained step-level exploratory dynamics.

contributions.claim: RAPO is an RL framework that uses retrieval to expand exploration during Agentic RL training.
RAPO decomposes training into Hybrid-policy Agentic Rollout and Retrieval-aware Policy Optimization.
The framework combines step-level off-policy trace retrieval during reasoning with retrieval reward and importance shaping for policy-gradient estimation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe RAPO as a novel RL framework that introduces retrieval to expand exploration during training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a 5.0% average gain across fourteen datasets and three agentic reasoning tasks.
The authors report 1.2x faster training efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Agentic RL enables LLM agents to solve complex tasks through multi-step, tool-integrated reasoning.
Pure on-policy exploration limits agents to self-generated outputs, while trajectory-level use of off-policy signals misses step-level exploratory dynamics.
RAPO introduces retrieval-augmented exploration through hybrid-policy rollout and retrieval-aware policy optimization.
Retrieved step-level traces broaden reasoning, while retrieval reward and importance shaping stabilize and prioritize exploration.
The authors report gains across fourteen datasets and three tasks together with faster training.

source_observation.claim: The abstract identifies a limitation in pure on-policy exploration and proposes conditioning reasoning on retrieved off-policy step-level traces.

interpretation.claim: Fine-grained reuse of external reasoning behavior may broaden exploration beyond an agent's self-generated trajectories.

application.claim: For multi-step tool-using agents, consider incorporating external step-level traces into rollout while preserving explicit controls for how those traces influence optimization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers to agent settings, tasks, or data distributions beyond the reported evaluation.

unknowns: The fourteen datasets and three agentic reasoning tasks are not identified.
Baselines, evaluation protocols, metric definitions, and statistical uncertainty are not reported.
The source and construction of retrieved traces are not specified.
The computational conditions underlying the 1.2x training-efficiency figure are not specified.
